questions.question: When braking, weight moves to the front of your bike. What should you do?

options.text: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
Use more rear brake pressure.
Don't worry. Weight transfer won't affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: As you brake, slowly increase the pressure on the front brake lever. The bike's weight shifts forward to the front tire.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on a motorcycle?

options.text: Before the engine starts.
After the engine starts.
As far back on the seat as possible.
While holding onto the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: After the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should board after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the driver's control and hold onto the driver's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Block your escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoids blind spots and road hazards, and keeps an escape route open if danger appears. It should not block your escape route.

questions.question: For normal stops, what brakes should you use?

options.text: Only the rear brake.
Only the front brake.
Both the front and rear brakes.
Alternate between front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping, including normal, everyday stops.

questions.question: Before entering a turn, what should a rider do?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Lean their shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the center.
On the left side.
On the right side.
Anywhere in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This discourages the other driver from moving back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a cause of a wobble on your motorcycle?

options.text: Wrong tire pressure
Improper loading
Wrong accessories
Uneven road

questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not speed up to escape a wobble.

questions.question: What is one requirement for an effective eye or face shield?

options.text: It must fasten securely.
It must block all air flow.
Eyeglasses cannot fit under it.
It must limit side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: It must fasten securely.
questions.explanation: An effective shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: How do you brake with maximum stopping power in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum braking power comes from using both the front and rear brakes together. Neither wheel should lock up.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
Talk as much as they want.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk as much as they want.
questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet to help you focus on riding. They should get on after you start the engine, sit forward without crowding you, and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop a motorcycle?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake lever hard.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
Gradually increase pressure on the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: Brake smoothly and firmly. As you stop, more weight moves forward, giving the front wheel more traction. Use increasing pressure on the front brake and less pressure on the rear brake. Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Leave the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Try to use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve as separate actions. Do one, then do the other. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: If you must swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn your handlebars quickly.
Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handlebar grip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to go. To turn left, press the left grip, then press the right grip to straighten out. To turn right, press the right grip, then the left grip.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
The drinker's body weight
How often the drinker drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker drinks
questions.explanation: Three things affect BAC: how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and body weight. How often someone drinks does not affect their BAC. Never drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When packing items on a motorcycle, where should heavy items go?

options.text: Toward the front.
Toward the rear.
Behind the rear axle.
In front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the front.
questions.explanation: Pack heavy items toward the front of the load. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
They make objects look closer than they actually are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you. They make objects appear farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: If you brake while turning a curve, what happens?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be very careful. While leaning to turn, your tires use some of their grip for the turn. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: In a slow, tight turn, what should the rider do?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean at the same angle as your motorcycle. But in slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Ride in a single-file line.
The group will exit at the next turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in a group. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points with one finger, it means all riders should move into a single-file line.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look ahead.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Use only your mirrors.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How do you stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake hard and gradually increase the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Speed up before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching a dangerous area, like an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: How do you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: On a wet road, which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
The entire lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks collects in the center of the lane. This strip normally has good traction, but when wet, it becomes slippery. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride to the side and still stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: What should you do when riding through turns?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look ahead.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look ahead.
questions.explanation: Always look ahead through turns to where you want to go. Turn only your head to look, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When shifting into neutral.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When a stop sign is ahead.
When your turn signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: If a driver is following too closely behind you, flash your brake light before you start to slow down. This warns them that you are slowing down to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see better.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.
Give you an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you out of blind spots, away from wind blasts, and away from hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and should give you an escape route in case of danger.
